item.title: [The Brussels Times] For Brussels activists, speed dating is about more than finding love
item.dc:creator: The Brussels Times

item.content:encoded:
Dating as an activist can be difficult in Brussels. It’s a small, professional bubble where potential dates could share mutual friends or be current or former colleagues.
If your political views are important to you, dating apps and singles nights don’t make it any easier when there’s a growing political polarisation between the left and right.
“In the end, you spend most of your time just trying to filter out hundreds of people that you don’t have shared values with,” Cass Heldon, the organiser of the third Speed Dating for Activists event, told the Brussels Times.
“And it’s not to say that you can never date beyond your political spectrum, but it’s such a key part of your identity.”
Speed dating for activists has been met with high demand in Brussels. The event is organised by the Green Fix, a six-volunteer climate initiative that began as a newsletter by Heldon with over 5,500 subscribers on Substack. It describes itself as “your bullshit-free roundup of climate justice, feminist and decolonial news and opportunities in Europe and beyond.”
Previous speed-dating editions had long wait lists, and attendance is capped at 50 participants. Tickets sold out last week, though the wait list was again left open, and the event will take place at an undisclosed bar in the Brussels city centre to prevent any unwanted crashers.
Dating in the age of political polarisation
However, the event has faced criticism. Heldon described getting comments online, typically from what she described as "angry men," arguing that the events are exclusionary and contribute to growing political polarisation and division between the left and the right.
“Of course, we do need a lot of dialogue across the political spectrum and we do see governments and corporations kind of propelling this polarisation,” Heldon said.
While she acknowledged the need to break down these barriers, she argued that not every aspect of life needs to be devoted to bridging a political divide. “And when it comes to dating and personal relationships,” Heldon said, “it really matters what your partner thinks about your views, your values.”
Third time's the charm
The Brussels Times spoke with Louis, a 29-year-old from Brussels who works in a shelter for victims of domestic violence and attended the previous speed-dating events. Though none of his matches led to romantic relationships, for Louis, the event was still a success.
Even if they don’t find love, activist speed dating is a way for people in Brussels' activist and NGO circles to meet outside their professional networks. For an introvert like Louis, these events can make future networking and building community easier.
“I was like, okay, I'm not going to date those people,” he said, “but I know I'm going to meet them at some events afterwards, and it would be nice to see them again and to have discussions.”
Success stories
When asked about any success stories, Heldon admitted that she couldn’t name any long-term relationships that arose from previous events. “You know, I’m not entirely sure because they don’t tell me,” she said. “They should keep me in CC.”
However, there were matches who continued to go on several dates, and there are previous participants who didn’t register for the third event because they’re now in relationships. Even if it wasn’t because of the speed-dating event, Heldon said, she would like to think it was a step in their journey.
However, new friendships have certainly been formed, and attendees continue to go to other events the Green Fix hosts, “so I count that as a success,” she said.
And for the speed-dating events overall? She said they've been a success.
“I think, you know, when you go to a speed dating, the success isn't necessarily in whether you find someone that you fall in love with and stay together forever. The success is whether you had a good time and whether you hung out with good people.”

item.content:encoded:
GREENFIELD — Before going to the polls on Nov. 3, the League of Women Voters of Franklin County made sure voters got to know the nine ballot questions better during a speed dating-style information session.
Thursday’s event, hosted by the league and Greenfield Community College, saw volunteers provide information to the roughly 30 attendees about what it means to vote “yes” or “no,” and the arguments for and against each ballot question. While the League of Women Voters of Massachusetts has taken a stance on some of the questions, Thursday’s event was explicitly nonpartisan and informational only, according to Marie Gauthier, president of the League of Women Voters of Franklin County.
Tables were set up at GCC, acting as stations for all nine questions. Each round gave five minutes for the presenters to share their information and take questions before Gauthier rang cowbells to signal the transition.
This style of voter engagement is something that Gauthier said is not new for the league, which hosted an event called “Candi-dating Night” for voters to get to know candidates for the 2017 municipal elections in Greenfield. She added that it’s a “fun and interactive” way to learn.
“There are a lot of ballot question events, and I just wanted to do something that was more engaging and might get people out,” Gauthier said, noting that the program also helps members of the league learn about the questions.
According to Commonwealth Beacon, this year’s number of ballot questions is nearly record-breaking, as the 1994 election also had nine questions, the most in the state’s history. During that election, five of the nine questions were accepted by voters. If a MassINC Polling Group and CommonWealth Beacon poll from September ends up reflecting the results in November, eight of the nine questions would receive a “yes” vote, while Question 8, the recreational marijuana repeal, would be the single “no.”
The ballot questions will ask voters to tackle a range of themes in legislative accountability and personal liberties. Question 1 seeks to expand public records law to the Legislature and governor’s office. Question 8 asks to repeal recreational marijuana legalization. The format of primary elections is up for change in Question 3, along with tax reform in Question 5.
Gauthier said the hope is that even if attendees didn’t have their minds made up, they would “have the tools to make those decisions” by the end of the night.
The presenters used numerous sources in their research, Gauthier said, including CommonWealth Beacon and the Tufts University Center for State Policy Analysis.
At the tables, some presenters, like Nicola Shipman, used visual aids to help best describe the question they were presenting. Shipman was tasked with Question 7, known as the starter-home question.
Question 7 asks voters if they’d like to relax zoning regulations for single-family homes in areas with public water and sewer, which would streamline the permitting process for homes to be built on smaller lots.
With her posters in hand, one for “yes” and one for “no,” she detailed some of the key arguments for both sides while taking questions from those at the table. Some of the discussion for one group with Shipman was about the state movement toward encouraging creation of accessory dwelling units and if this question impacts those goals, or skepticism about the question’s relevance to western Massachusetts, whose communities are more spread out and with private water and sewer, compared to out east.
One of the voters in attendance, Patricia Stevenson of Shelburne, said she came to the speed-dating event with her mind made up on some of the questions, especially Question 9, which she plans to vote “yes” on. This question seeks to uphold the state’s 2024 gun law, and a “yes” vote would preserve that law, while a “no” vote would repeal it and bring the state back to pre-2024 gun regulations.
“I’m not opposed to people owning a gun, but those assault rifles should be banned as far as I’m concerned,” Stevenson said. “That’s a question I have no problem [with].”
Stevenson expressed her gratitude to the League of Women Voters of Franklin County for hosting the event and educating people.
“I think these ballot questions, the way they’re written, they’re very legal-like and it’s very hard for people to understand,” she said, “so I think having this really helped inform us to be a better voter.”
Those seeking to register to vote, check their voter registration status or access the red booklet from the Secretary of State’s Office detailing each of the nine ballot questions can visit sec.state.ma.us.

item.content:encoded:
We’ve got a one-stop guide to find out about all the dating events happening in Singapore – from speed dates to intentional dinners.
Dating events in Singapore happen more frequently than you think! With the rise of in-person social events, we’re clearly not the only ones craving some real-life socialising. And for the members of the lonely hearts club, you’ve likely exhausted your dating app matches. How about trying something new with a little in-person chit-chat? All you have to do is find one that catches your eye (the same way your new beau will).
Culture Sg never disappoints when it comes to social events in Singapore. Branching out from Above 30 Club comes SomeoneNew, a place for all 30-somethings and up to meet like-minded people. Because we all know as you get older, making friends gets ridiculously harder. The collective is hosting its first singles’ event, and you have two ways to meet your match – approach the cutie across the bar or leave it up to fate with a questionnaire. And there’ll be plenty of games to keep things interesting along the way.
When: 21 October 2026, 7.30pm to 10.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $30; includes one drink
Where: SomeoneNew: Love edition, Rasa Space, 9 Raffles Place, Singapore 048619
Hey, Gen Zs. We haven’t forgotten about you, and neither has the team at Type Mixers. What started as a desire to ditch the dating apps and to “do it for the plot” soon turned into regular themed gatherings to put singles into a room to see what happens. And then, strangers became friends while sparks flew. Sounds like a pretty magical journey to us! You can also join the fun by keeping an eye out on the team’s social media pages for updates.
For the month of October, it’s no surprise that we’re getting another Halloween-themed mixer! This time, you’re getting a mystery match, secret identity, and a hidden mission. Come dressed as either a devil or an angel and enjoy tarot reading, snap photos at a photo booth, sip Halloween-themed drinks, and meet a special someone along the way.
When: 30 October 2026, 7.30pm to 11pm
How much: Tickets start from $48 for ladies and $55 for men; pre-registration required
Where: Type Mixers: Angels & Devils, location revealed only to confirmed attendees
After its launch in 2024, the demand for Never Strangers events skyrocketed and clearly has no signs of coming down! As one of the first offline social event collectives to come about, the team has hosted a number of social events, from dating mixers to platonic dinners. If you want to be part of this cool kids club, register your details on the website, and you’ll be added to the guest list! Events are curated based on age, vibe, and interest, so you’ll be hand-picked for an event that’s catered to you.
The next edition of Never Strangers will be hosted on a yacht. AKA, the perfect opportunity for you to break out a cute swimsuit that hasn’t seen water in a hot minute. Sailing out of Keppel Bay, you’ll get to enjoy free-flow cocktails by Garage, games, and the classic algorithm match reveal before returning to the dock.
When: Hosts events monthly; yacht event on 24 October 2026, 3pm to 7pm
How much: Varies with each event
Where: Never Strangers, register online
Let us introduce you to Thursday; the biggest IRL dating app in the world. It’s less about the dating app itself and more about the in-person events. Because they care about getting you out the door to meet someone rather than spend your time endlessly matching. All you have to do is pick your city and you can pick from a tidy list of events happening in your area.
We’ve already spotted a variety of singles’ mixers you can join depending on what your vibe is! Enter a game of mystery mini golf, head to a rooftop bar for conversations with stunning city views, or enter a Halloween-themed encounter.
When: Various dates
How much: Ticket costs vary with each event
Where: Thursday, locations vary
From the same crew who brought you the dating series Maybe It’s You is The Stupid Cupid. The team will be hosting its first singles mixer, taking the dating experience offline, putting the same thoughtfulness and love into it. There is a strict vetting process you’ll have to go through if you want to participate. But this means the crowd will be extra curated to ensure a good vibe.
When: 1 November 2026, 7pm till late
How much: Free admission; registration required, closes 18 October 2026
Where: The Stupid Cupid’s Singles’ Mixer, location revealed to confirmed attendees
You’d be surprised at how good the vibes are at a TCM-inspired bar. So good, that you’ll even spot The One sitting across from you! The bar will be hosting a specially curated singles’ day dinner for a small group of curious bar-goers. As you chat over food, you’ll participate in shared activities and little acts of service that keep the conversation flowing. More details are set to be released, so stay tuned.
When: 11 November 2026, 6pm
How much: To be confirmed
Where: Singles’ Day at Synthesis, #01-643, Suntec City, 3 Temasek Boulevard, Singapore 038983
Think you’ve got what it takes to help your friend bait a date at Fishbowl? Then sign yourselves up for the latest singles’ pitch event happening in October. You, as your BFF’s wingman, have to convince a crowd full of strangers why your friend is the best date candidate out there. Prepare a three-minute presentation and sell ‘em with your best elevator pitch. Psst: show off your Coffee Meets Bagel profile, and you can get 10% off your drinks!
When: 23 October 2026, 7.30pm to 9.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $30 (includes one free drink)
Where: Flying Fish: Singles’ Pitch Night, Wingman Edition, Rasa Space, 9 Raffles Place, Singapore 048619
Let’s be real here – we could all use a session of puppy yoga to relieve some stress. But this session is specifically for the single dog parents out there. Use this as an excuse to get your pupper out for a playdate, but with yoga mats and (hopefully) no awkward small talk. Get to know other yoga participants as you stretch, or wait till after the session during your own social hour. Who knows, maybe your furkid could find the love of their life here too.
When: 21 November 2026, 4pm to 5.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $70
Where: Dog Owners Yoga Date, Gravity by Noir, 144 Robinson Road, Singapore 068908
Expect a little sugar and a lot of spice in this Dia de los Meurtos-esque singles’ mixer. Come dressed in theme with touches of marigolds, skulls, and dark romance to impress and let the night unfold. If you’re attached, feel free to come find friends too! You’ll be given traffic light-style wristbands that indicate your status so people know what you’re looking for. Then simply let the night unfold and see what it has in store for you.
When: 22 October 2026, 8pm to 10pm
How much: $55 per person (includes 2 alcoholic drinks and snacks); pre-registration required
Where: Deadly Chemistry: A Mexican Singles’ Night, Mami’s Tamales, 55 Keong Saik Road, Singapore 089158
For singles aged 30 to 50 years old, this is a dating event in Singapore for you. This isn’t any ordinary rooftop bar in the city. It’s actually about to turn into a venue for conversation where sparks come alive. If you need a sign from the universe, turn to the tarot reading corner and get a mini reading on love and romance. And as you bathe in the golden hour light, prepare yourself for side quests! Prompts will be sent to your phone, giving you an excuse to talk to the stranger you’ve been eyeing all evening.
When: 22 October 2026, 6pm to 9pm
How much: Tickets start from $60 for ladies & $50 for men; includes one free drink
Where: Rooftop Connections at Truth or Dare, 11 North Canal Road, Singapore 048824
Everyone talks about small and intentional groups, but what about a social night for those of us who love being in a crowd? One Tile Away frequently hosts mahjong games meant for singles looking for love or players looking for extra mahjong kakis. The upcoming socials are hosted in larger groups, and you’ll be split into your tables to meet some new people. And yes, beginners are welcome to attend and facilitators will be on-site to guide you through the game.
When: 21, 28 & 29 October 2026
How much: Ticket prices vary with each event
Where: One Tile Away: A Social Mixer, multiple locations including Enclosed and *Scape
Give your creative side an opportunity to shine at this neon singles party happening just before Halloween! This glow-in-the-dark art jamming experience doesn’t even need you to be a painter. You’ll be guided by instructors the whole step of the way, and walk home with a glowing masterpiece. And while you’re at it, mingle with fellow singles and get a conversation flowing.
When: 30 October 2026, 7.30pm to 9.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $58; all art materials provided
Where: Singles Neon Party, #02-01, Scuro, 79 Kampong Bahru Road, Singapore 169377
We already know the pickleball trend is here to stay, so why not use your new hobby to meet some new people? Come for a social game and meet new people through a mix of friendly games and off-court conversations. No experience necessary! You’ll be rotated through different groups to meet different players, and have plenty of time to mingle after the games. Paddles and balls provided, so just come as you are.
When: 6 November 2026, 8pm to 10.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $18 for ladies & $58 for men
Where: Play!Pickle: Match & Mingle, #04-27, 756 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534626
You know what’s a great way to break the ice with a cute stranger? Letting your furkid do the approaching! Bettr Coffee is hosting a singles’ pitch night, and you’re more than welcome to bring your pupper to its pet-friendly space at The Foundry. Don’t have a pet or don’t intend to bring them along? No worries, because you’re still welcome to join and meet new people regardless. Seeing all the pets in one place is a fabulous bonus.
When: 16 October 2026, 7pm to 9pm
How much: Tickets start from $25
Where: Singles Pitch Night: Pets & Pawrents Edition, Bettr Coffee, The Foundry, 11 Prinsep Link, Singapore 187949
If you need an excuse to enjoy a date and some good wine, look no further than Vivino’s singles’ day mixer. You’ll be treated to three glasses of wine to help smoothen things along. And don’t worry if you’re a little shy, because a dating coach will be on-site to help provide some structure! Think: activities that’ll actually get you talking and real dating tips.
When: 11 November 2026, 7pm to 8pm
How much: Tickets start from $45
Where: Vivino Singles Mixer, #01-44B, Raffles City, 252 North Bridge Road, Singapore 179103
We think Goodbye, Alibi’s cosy space makes for a fab date night spot – so why not use it to try finding The One? Cure hump day with a cheeky drink and meet-cute with a small group of strangers. This means conversations will go beyond the usual small talk, with curated ice breakers, and ice cold drinks. This event is also all-inclusive, so feel free to come as you are and with an open mind.
When: Every first Wednesday of the month; 4 November 2026 & 2 December 2026
How much: Tickets start from $10 for ladies and $35 for men
Where: Small group dating at Goodbye, Alibi, 53A Duxton Road, Singapore 089517
Looking for love? Let’s see if dating events in Singapore can help you out!
Speed dating is an event structure where you’ll have short, one-to-one conversations with potential matches. Each round lasts only a few minutes before you rotate to the next person. After the whole session is over, you’re usually invited to speak with people who you’d like to see again.
Prices vary depending on what kind of activities are being hosted and the venue. You can expect dates to cost anywhere between $30 to $50 if they involve activities. For curated dinners, you may pay upwards of $100.
Yes, feel free to join even if you’re not ready for a serious relationship. Dating events are meant for people to meet, and not everyone will commit to something long-term. However, it’s important to communicate this with the people you meet.
You’d be surprised by the number of dating events catering to people aged 30 and up! Keep your eye out for collectives like Never Strangers and SomeoneNew, which host gatherings for people above 30.
Yes, there are! Most dating events welcome people of all orientations, and often disclaim it in the event descriptions. If you’re uncertain, you can message the organisers to double check.

item.content:encoded:
They grew up swiping, but Manchester’s twentysomethings are ghosting dating apps in favour of an old-school solution making a comeback across the city: speed dating.
Mid20s, founded by Jonah Gray and Evie Carricker, has sold out all 41 of its speed dating events for 23 to 27-year-olds since launching in the city last summer.
Their events have attracted more than 1,000 Mancunian singles, who have collectively been on over 5,000 dates, resulting in more than 400 romantic matches.
Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter
The idea came after Jonah and Evie, who met by chance on a coach from Bristol to Manchester, bonded over their frustrations with modern dating culture and the lack of opportunities for young people to meet in person.
Jonah, who previously organised music events and raves, said the pair shared a disdain for dating apps that led them to create an alternative to digital dating for young people.
“What was at first maybe a nice idea, and maybe seemed like something that could help connect people, has now made people even further apart,” he said.
“There’s an abundance of choice, and I think it creates this real expendable viewpoint of a person.”
He said in-person speed dating solved that problem.
“Within five minutes, you’ve met someone, had a chat. On paper, you’re dating 12 people for the price of one.
“You’re being precious with your time and energy whilst meeting loads of people.”
Demand for the events has grown quickly. What began as a single Manchester night now runs close to fortnightly in the city and has expanded to Sheffield and Leeds, with tickets regularly selling out within minutes of release.
Each event typically hosts around 30 people, who take part in five-minute dates with other attendees. At the end of the night, guests submit the names of up to three people they would like to see again romantically.
But the founders said the friendships formed at the events had become just as significant as the romantic matches.
“I think we underestimated how much of it that would be,” Evie said.
“We’ve got huge groups of people who’ve all met through our events.”
They said feedback had been overwhelmingly positive, with 91 per cent of attendees rating their experience five stars and groups often continuing to socialise well beyond the scheduled dating slots.
The pair also vet every attendee before issuing tickets in a bid to create a safe and welcoming environment. “It’s amazing how consistently lovely the people we attract are,” Jonah said.
The founders said they hoped more people who were hesitant about attending would give the events a try.
“I just wish people who were on the fence would just do it,” Jonah said. “We get so many people who say they were so nervous, they almost dropped out, and then they had a brilliant time. The worst thing that’ll happen is you end up with a funny story for the group chat,” Evie added.
The next Mid20s Manchester event, for lesbian, bisexual and queer women, will take place on Tuesday, September 22 at To Be Frank. A further event for men and women is planned for October 14 at Side Street.
Events are ticketed, with details available by messaging @mid__twenties on Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
SOUTH LAKE TAHOE, Calif. — The Rotary Club of South Lake Tahoe, the South Tahoe Association of REALTORS®, and Citizens for Integrity in Government will host a City Council Candidate Speed Dating Forum on October 1 at the STAOR building, located at 2307 James Avenue.
The event will begin at 6:00 p.m. and will offer community members an informal, interactive way to meet the candidates for South Lake Tahoe City Council.
Rather than using a traditional forum format in which candidates speak from a stage, candidates will rotate among small groups of community members seated throughout the room. During each timed round, candidates will briefly introduce themselves and answer questions from attendees. The format is intended to encourage direct conversation, meaningful interaction, and discussion of the issues affecting South Lake Tahoe.
Members of the public will remain seated while candidates rotate from table to table. By the end of the evening, each audience group will have an opportunity to meet and hear from every participating candidate.
The Candidate Speed Dating Forum is intended to provide voters with an engaging and accessible opportunity to learn more about the individuals seeking to represent them on the South Lake Tahoe City Council.
The event is open to the public. Doors will open at 5:45 p.m. and the program will begin promptly at 6:00 p.m.
EVENT DETAILS
City Council Candidate Speed Dating Forum
October 1, 2026
6:00 p.m.
STAOR Building
2307 James Avenue
South Lake Tahoe, California

Welcome, fans of fantasy and romantasy. You are invited to join a themed evening of speed dating in the worlds of magical realms, secret desires, creatures, forbidden glances, shadow daddies, and adventure. Costumes and/or festive attire encouraged. The non-traditional choose-your-own-adventure format includes lots of opportunities for connection and fun, such as flirty bingo, calling cards, tarot, and always lots of laughs.
Come solo, or with friends; you won’t have to date your friends (unless you want to). Expand your community, flirt with a crush, or just come for a night of merriment and silliness! Queer and enm-friendly, and welcoming to all orientations and expressions. All experience levels with fantasy and romantasy are welcome.
Delicious vittles and libations available for purchase from the affable hosts at Oran Mor Mead.

item.content:encoded:
From trainings to volunteering and paid gigs, find opportunities to get involved in Detroit every week — brought to you by the Detroit Documenters.
Detroit Heals Detroit is, as the saying goes, “doing the most,” — from its free giveaways, showers and laundry service to after-school programs and neighborhood parades. Now it’s hiring for several positions and offering free transportation to participate in local public meetings. You have to know Detroit Documenters love that! Check out the many opportunities to get involved.
Happening soon
Keep It in the Family
Apply by Wednesday, Sept. 23
Woodbridge neighborhood homeowners 55 and older can apply for estate planning and home repair assistance. Get details on the program, including eligibility requirements, and apply now. 
Restore Rouge Park Prairie
Friday, Sept. 25, 5 p.m.
North Prairie Trail, 14500-14800 W. Outer Drive, Detroit
Help Friends of Rouge Park revive the habitat for flowers and pollinators in Rouge Park. Stick around for a sunset prairie hike. Sign up now. 
Community Bio Blitz
Saturday, Sept. 26, 10-11 a.m.
Eliza Howell Park, 23751 Fenkell Ave., Detroit
Join Sidewalk Detroit for a plant ID walk through Eliza Howell Park. Bring a cell phone with data, wear long pants and boots. Bug spray recommended.
Community Policy Fair
Saturday, Sept. 26, 11 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Wayne County Community College District, 801 W. Fort St., Detroit
Hopewell Church’s social justice ministry, Beyond 4 Walls, is connecting residents with policymakers, advocates, agency leaders and community organizations working in economic empowerment, housing, health and education. Because “policy is personal,” there will not be a traditional panel. Instead, residents will be able to engage directly, ask questions, connect with organizations and better understand how policy decisions show up in everyday life. Register now.
Expungement Fair
Saturday, Sept. 26, noon to 4 p.m.
Perfecting Church, 7616 E. Nevada Ave., Detroit
Learn more about clearing your criminal record, and apply to get started with the expungement process (which typically takes about eight months). Register now. Attorneys and law students can also apply to volunteer. 
Repair Cafe Volunteer Orientation
Saturday, Sept. 26, 1 to 4 p.m.
B. Nektar Meadery, 1511 Jarvis St., Ferndale
If you know how to sew or fix things — from clothes and jewelry to appliances and laptops — volunteer with the Repair Cafe! Their motto? “Let’s fix your stuff, together!” Pull up to learn how it works.
Detroit Solidarity Economy Assembly
Sunday, Sept. 27, 3-5 p.m.

The position pays $16 an hour for 10-15 hours a week from mid-October through December. Get details and send a résumé to info@nextchapterbookstore.com to apply.

The Coalition for Property Tax Justice is collecting stories of Detroit property owners to build an archive of tax injustice. Have you experienced tax foreclosure? Share your story.

Regional Freight Plan

BridgeDetroit seeks to connect with local high school students ages 13-18 to understand how they consume news, what issues matter to them and how they want to engage civically. The survey will inform BridgeDetroit’s coverage and events. Learn more and take the survey.

Be Well Beautiful People is leading a citywide effort to understand how residents feel about their well-being. The survey “will help shape future systems” that support collective well-being. Take the survey.

Join a walking group and exercise with friends you haven’t met yet. Through September, meet up for a one-hour walk at eight city parks, the Joe Louis Greenway and the riverfront. All participants get a T-shirt. Check out the schedule.

The Furniture Bank of Metro Detroit needs donations of mattresses, sofas and other home goods in clean, working condition for families in need. Residents of Wayne, Oakland or Macomb counties can submit furniture donations online and schedule a free pickup.

item.content:encoded:
- Published
The food distribution charity Felix spent £5.6m last year collecting surplus produce, and getting it to the community organisations it supports.
Richard Smith, director of food innovation at Felix, said: "These are costs we cannot cut. Without our logistics, this food would never reach the millions who need it most."
But a new platform dubbed "speed dating for trucks" has been launched to reduce those costs.
Using AI technology to bring together logistics providers, retailers and manufacturers, it matches spare haulage capacity with surplus food collections.
Early trials of the new software and system have already saved the charity money.
Smith added: "The benefits are all there - real and instant."
Deliveries of surplus food arrive all day at the Felix depot and kitchen in Poplar, east London.
It is sorted in the warehouse and redistributed to charities across London working to ease food poverty.
Until now, the administration has fallen to the logistics team at Felix (formerly the Felix Project), which books a haulier and pays for the transportation.
The costs soon add up.
Nicola Robinson, director of Alliance Food Sourcing (AFS) - a coalition of leading food companies - said: "Felix spent in 2025, £5.6m on 80,000 pallets, and three quarters of that cost was coming from third-party logistics companies.
"We thought we could take a look at that and if we tap into the spare capacity that we know exists within UK road hauliers, then we could put that to good use."
According to the Department for Transport, about 30% of all HGV journeys have spare capacity.
Using AI technology, the platform matches that space in lorries with deliveries to the Felix depots - hence the speed dating nickname.
Early trials with the food producer Greencore have led to a twice-weekly delivery of milk going to the Felix depot.
That route alone is projected to save the charity £20,000 a year.
Smith said: "The milk comes in every single week with very light touch from Felix, so we're barely getting involved.
"Now this is just a locked-in route, it happens every single week - that milk lands here and is back out to charities within 24 hours."
Currently, Greencore offers the service free of charge.
Darren Binns, head of logistics at Greencore, said: "There is an element of cost here but we think that we can absorb that cost, use the extra space that we have to do the right thing, to move surplus food into Felix's charity network."
Sainsbury's and logistics provider GXO have identified a further 10 routes for moving Felix food, with estimated annual savings of around £170,000.
Tesco, M&S and supply chain company Gist are also involved in the project, offering free consultancy and logistics support.
Data from the Trust for London showed that food insecurity has risen by 23% in London over the past two years.
Alongside the rise in need, transportation costs have gone up, and this is at a time when our changing climate sees demands that we reduce carbon emissions.
If the new platform is upscaled, AFS said it could save Felix £1m a year, as well as reduce road miles.
It said it would transform the way different sectors work, and urged more in the food industry to support the project.

item.content:encoded:
POCATELLO, Idaho (KIFI) – Pocatello spiced up the political scene with a non-partisan “Meet Your Candidates: Speed Dating-style” night at the Idaho State University ballroom tonight.
Voters were able to meet 10 of the 12 candidates running for Idaho’s Legislature District 29 in Pocatello and District 28 representing Chubbuck and surrounding areas.
The activity was sponsored by the Idaho State University Political Science Club, Southeast Idaho Citizens for Democracy and Braver Angels.
“We'd like to give the participants, the voters, an experience of meeting candidates up close and personal," said Braver Angels Organizer Dr. Michael Jindra.
Residents asked questions for 15 minutes to each of the five candidates running from their region. 
Voters inquired about data centers, healthcare, Medicare cuts, protecting public land, relations with the Shoshone-Bannock tribe and more.
"There's a lot of toxicity in politics right now through advertisements, through the internet," Jindra said. "This is a personal event that helps people get to know candidates face-to-face, and I think that kind of helps tone it down a little bit."
Candidates who participated are starred:
Idaho Senate District 28
*Jim Guthrie (R) and *Mandy Peace (D)
Idaho House of Representatives District 28 Seat A
*Kim Jackman (D) and Rick Cheatum (R) 
Idaho House of Representatives District 28 Seat B
*Dan Garner (R) and *Jayson Meline (D)
Idaho Senate District 28
*James Ruchti (D) and John Crowder (R)
Idaho House of Representatives District 29 Seat A
*Dustin Manwaring (R) and *Mary Shea (D)
Idaho House of Representatives District 29 Seat B
*Nate Roberts (D) and *Jennifer Miles (R)
Local News 8 will publish in-depth reports with each candidate in the weeks before the general election on November 3, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Passionate Northampton fundraiser branches out to host crafters carousel workshop – think speed dating but with crafts
A passionate fundraiser in Northampton has branched out to host a new style of event called a crafters carousel workshop, which she has described as speed dating but with crafts.
Natalie Wood is known for organising charity events in memory of her late brother Sam Grove. These raise money and awareness for Northamptonshire Mind to support mental health and address the stigma around alcohol addiction.
Sam tragically passed away at the age of 30 in March 2023 and Natalie has organised multiple successful community events, including a winter shopping experience at The Elgar Centre and summer gatherings at The George Inn.
Natalie has now broadened her horizons to host events under the umbrella organisation of Natalie Wood Events, and the crafters carousel workshop is taking place from 10am until 1pm on October 18 at The Brampton Halt.
This will be a relaxed morning when attendees will get to try four different crafts with a brilliant group of makers. You will spend 30 minutes at each station before moving onto the next, and you do not need to consider yourself crafty to come along.
This is an introductory and experimental workshop, with a focus on simply having a go, trying something new and seeing what you enjoy.
The first station will be needle felting with Ali Edwards from Fuzzycrumbs, during which attendees will make a small pumpkin from 100 percent wool. The next is centred around essential oils and making your own roller ball with Sabrina Smart.
Kerry Mattock Tobin from Kerry’s Creative Therapeutic Workshops will help the crafters get hands on with clay, and Lizzie Foster from Hoglet House Crafts will be teaching the basics of paper quilling.
Because no morning of crafting is complete without refreshments, there will be cakes and drinks too. Tickets are £30 per person and include the four taster sessions, all the materials you need, your creations to take home, and the chance to try something outside of your comfort zone.
There will also be the opportunity to purchase some of the crafters’ kits to take away, so if you discover something you love, you can carry on creating at home. Spaces are limited so secure your ticket while they are still available.

item.content:encoded:
I’ve just tried blind speed-dating. Missed it in my twenties. Was too square.
Now in a spasm of late forties’ angst I’ve spent hours calling total strangers trying to make them like me.
I didn’t ever think I’d end up speed-dating. Didn’t think the wife would approve – or that would-be girl for that matter. I’m a bit out of practice – and out of shape let’s face it. But after this week, like a 49-year-old virgin on a first date, I’ve become something of a silver-tongued suitor. Just not on the right people. I’m told girls love questions. It shows you care. But I’ve discovered that civil servants on the end of a phone don’t. Even if they’re called Shahida.
My wife Tetiana needed a share code. It’s an electronic ID. A random mix of numbers and letters the government gives you if you’re not a citizen so you can work, rent or, in our case, get a mortgage. They should just tattoo it on your arm when you first arrive at Dover. There’s an idea Nigel.
Now, Tetiana has been in the country since 2009. She has Indefinite Leave to Remain. Stamped in her passport – two passports ago. She’s allowed in even though in her fur coat she looks like a Romanian people smuggler. She can be let loose on a mental health clinic but she can’t vote. Then three months into the remortgaging process, our mortgage advisor suddenly tells us they don’t accept paper visas. Although they did five years ago. You need a share code.
How do you get a share code? First, you set up a UKVI – UK Visas and Immigration – online account. Then they make you shlep all the way to Croydon to give your biometrics. It’s deliberate. If the office was in Hove, no one would ever leave the country. But who would want to stay in the UK after going to Croydon? In reality, most people who go to Croydon for a visa never actually leave. Because, trouble is, once Rick Deckard has bagged up your blood, hair, toenail clippings and fingerprints, you’re in no fit state to go anywhere else. So that’s Croydon.
And then you wait. And wait. Now a mortgage has a deadline. If you think you’re clobbered by your interest rate now, wait till you go on the standard variable rate. We had until September 23. Where was our share code? Silly me. Who’s going to catch any Home Office civil servant worth their salt working in August? Or even in England. I started to look up by-elections in Scotland to help make ends meet.
So, deep breath, we decide to phone UKVI. This is where speed dating skills come in handy. If Ovid was alive today, he wouldn’t write about the Minotaur – that horned cow at the centre of a labyrinth. No. He’d write about UKVI phone options. Because before you get to impress anyone with your wit, you need to press number 4. Then number 2. Then number 4. Then number 4 again. Then number 2. There are more numbers called out than during a night at Mecca bingo. Advisors are more protected from foreign reach than our gold bullion under Threadneedle Street.
It wouldn’t be so bad if it wasn’t a different advisor each time. “Calls may be recorded for training and data protection purposes.” Not to actually relieve you from having to tell them your problem all over again each time. And that’s before you’ve got past security. How long is your inside leg? What’s your cat’s middle name? Someone suddenly speaks: “How can I help you?” Can I remember how to speak English? “My wife needs a share code.” I hope he can smell my aftershave. Can pheromones travel down the phone line? “Have you got a UKVI account?” “Yes.” “Hang on a minute.”
Something in his voice told me this potential lover would never find my wife’s electronic data. My wife and I decide to tag team. The music stops and it’s time to move on. By the end of the night, no one’s marked my score card. Not even the wife.
All I can say is Tetiana must have more experience kissing frogs than me. However she wooed him, it worked. She probably chanced upon someone on day release from some luxury hotel that provides all day breakfast. With the speed and grace of a concierge at the Ritz, it took this marvel of productivity fewer than five minutes to fix my wife’s share code.
You can order swarms of bees on Amazon but if the state loses your data, it’s like looking for a yellow Lego brick in a children’s sand pit. Pity help us when the replicants take over.
Alistair McNair is Leader of the Conservatives on Brighton and Hove City Council.

item.content:encoded:
"Les gens cherchent plus un emploi que la formation" : des candidats de tous âges en quête de nouvelles opportunités professionnelles au speed dating de l’emploi

Le speed dating de l’emploi, organisé ce mardi à l’espace Cazot à Alès, attire un public varié, allant des jeunes en quête de premier emploi aux seniors en reconversion. L’événement permet aux entreprises et organismes de formation de rencontrer directement les candidats, offrant des opportunités du CAP au BTS dans divers secteurs.

C’était le défi proposé par le réseau Territoire, emploi, solidarité alésienne (Tesa). Un speed dating de l’emploi organisé ce mardi à l’espace Cazot, à Alès (Gard), qui ne rassemble pas que des jeunes à la recherche d’un premier emploi ou d’une formation. Sur place, des parcours variés, avec des candidats venus chercher un poste, mais aussi des pistes pour la suite de leur vie professionnelle.

"On arrive à recruter des candidats", explique Ludo Lombardi de L & B Coaching, alors que le rendez-vous permet aux entreprises et aux organismes de formation d’échanger directement avec les personnes présentes. Un public qui, selon Céline Ringot de CFA-Ecole Cévenole, est "divers, de tout âge". L’occasion de présenter des formations "du CAP au BTS", notamment dans différents secteurs professionnels.

Des profils divers

Parmi les visiteurs, une femme de 60 ans était notamment venue pour "chercher des idées" et pouvoir "se projeter". Un profil qui illustre une autre réalité de la recherche d’emploi : celle de personnes qui, après plusieurs années de vie professionnelle, cherchent elles aussi une nouvelle direction.

À lire aussi : "Faciliter la rencontre entre demandeurs d’emploi et entreprises… " : un grand job dating attendu à Alès pour la rentrée

"Les gens cherchent plus un emploi que la formation", observe par ailleurs Valérie, pour la Chambre de Métiers et de l’Artisanat du Gard. Mais derrière cette recherche, les situations restent différentes : certains veulent travailler rapidement, d’autres se renseignent avant de choisir une formation ou d’envisager une reconversion.

Sin embargo, el mundo de los oficios manuales no parece dejar de atraer a los habitantes de la cuenca, ya sea que salgan de la escuela o se conviertan en profesionales. "Y en esto, la Inteligencia Artificial nunca nos reemplazará", sonríe Céline Ringot.

item.content:encoded:
Cinque minuti per innamorarsi della ricerca! Mettiti comodo, scegli il tuo tavolo e preparati a un faccia a faccia ravvicinato con la scienza. Gli Speed Dating con la Scienza sono incontri lampo dove curiosità e scoperta si fondono: nessuna lezione accademica, solo il racconto vivo di chi esplora il nostro pianeta ogni giorno. Il tempo scorre, le domande corrono… tu a quale tavolo ti siederai?

1) Vulcani nel mondo e in Italia: un viaggio tra i vulcani d’Italia e del mondo per raccontare come la ricerca

scientifica non si limita a studiare i vari processi eruttivi ma raggiunge comunità che vivono in territori unici e spesso complessi, dal punto di vista geografico, ambientale e culturale.

2) Le più grandi bufale sui terremoti (e perché continuiamo a crederci): Si possono prevedere i terremoti? Gli animali sentono in anticipo le scosse? Attraverso brevi confronti in modalità speed date, i partecipanti potranno porre domande direttamente ai ricercatori, discutere dubbi e curiosità e scoprire come funziona la ricerca scientifica.

3) Sotto il mare, oltre i ghiacciai. Racconti di ricerca scientifica in ambienti estremi: Dagli abissi oceanici più oscuri alle distese di ghiaccio dell’Antartide: la ricerca scientifica è la vera esplorazione moderna. In questo speed date faremo un viaggio tra scienza, avventura e meraviglia nei luoghi più remoti e affascinanti della Terra.

4) GNSS ai confini del Mondo: come monitorare i ghiacci estremi: I Poli subiscono, più di ogni altro luogo del nostro pianeta, i cambiamenti climatici che stanno provocando uno scioglimento rapido dei ghiacci. I satelliti del Global Navigation Satellite System (quelli che chiamiamo GPS e usiamo ogni giorno), nati per dirci dove andare, oggi hanno un nuovo ruolo nel monitoraggio dell’ambiente artico. Misurare quanta neve cade ogni anno e vigilare sulla salute del ghiaccio marino. Una tecnologia quotidiana che diventa strumento per monitorare il futuro del nostro clima.

Justine (L’amour est dans le pré) interrompt brusquement son speed dating avec Audran : “Je ne peux pas rester”

Lors du nouvel épisode de L’amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi 14 septembre sur M6, Justine a rencontré ses prétendants. Alors qu’elle faisait la connaissance d’Audran, la jeune femme ne s’est pas sentie bien et a soudainement quitté la péniche.

Un moment pour le moins mouvementé. Après Vincent, son ami de longue date, Justine a pu se lancer dans l’étape des speed datings. Lors du nouvel épisode de L’amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi 14 septembre sur M6, la jeune femme de 34 ans a donné rendez-vous à cinq prétendants sur la péniche Quai Liberté à Liberté. Dépanneur automobile de 27 ans, Audran a été le premier à se lancer dans le bain. Alors qu’il dévoilait les raisons qui l’ont poussé à écrire à la pétillante propriétaire d’une ferme pédagogique, cette dernière a rapidement coupé court à leur échange. «Attends, ne bouge pas. Je ne peux pas rester sur le bateau», a-t-elle lancé, avant de prendre la fuite. Une situation qui a laissé sans voix Karine Le Marchand, qui suivait avec attention ce premier tête-à-tête au côté de Vincent. «Elle est partie !» Face à la surprise de l’animatrice, l’apiculteur a indiqué que Justine a «le mal de mer».

Bien que n’étant pas au meilleur de sa forme, la candidate s’est empressée de retrouver Audran pour poursuivre leur discussion. «Je suis désolée. Est-ce que tu peux te mettre en face comme ça, je ne vois pas l’eau qui est derrière toi», lui a-t-elle demandé, avant de le rassurer : «C’est une horreur mais c’est bon. C’est hyper mal poli, je suis désolée.» Alors qu’elle tentait de reprendre le fil de la conversation, Justine s’est une nouvelle fois éclipsée pour prendre l’air, laissant seul son soupirant. «Le pauvre. C’est la catastrophe. Ce n’est jamais arrivé dans toute l’histoire de L’amour est dans le pré !», a-t-elle indiqué avant de mettre fin à ces dix minutes interminables de speed dating. Si Audran était satisfait de cette rencontre, il en a été tout autre pour Justine.

Passer la publicité

Justine (L’amour est dans le pré) déçue par sa rencontre avec Audran : “Le problème, c’est sa taille”

À l’issue de cet «entretien historique», Karine Le Marchand s’est empressée de retrouver Justine pour un petit débriefing. Dès l’arrivée de la mère d’Alya, la candidate est revenue sur son malaise mais aussi sur un détail qui l’a quelque peu déçu. Si elle souhaite rencontrer un homme aussi grand qu’elle, Audran ne répond malheureusement pas à ce critère. «Le problème, c’est sa taille», a-t-elle avoué, avant d’être coupée net par la présentatrice : «Mais à quel moment on parle on parle de la taille d’un mec ? Là, tu nous l’as castré pour les 30 prochaines années !»

Après cette remarque, le constat a été sans appel pour Justine. «Je lui ai fait le pire date de sa vie». Pour éviter que ce scénario ne se reproduise, Karine Le Marchand lui a proposé d’installer une table dehors. Une suggestion que la principale intéressée a préféré décliner, au grand dam de la présentatrice. Reste à savoir si la suite des speed datings sera aussi chaotique.

item.content:encoded:
L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : “Ça m’a vraiment déçue !” Pourquoi Justine a très mal vécu son speed-dating ?

Publié le Par Drifa Maza

Ce lundi 14 septembre 2026, Justine sera au cœur de l’intrigue amoureuse dans L’Amour est dans le pré, diffusée sur M6. Toutefois, la candidate n’a pas exactement vécu l’aventure à laquelle elle s’attendait. Pourquoi l’étape du speed dating a-t-elle été compliquée pour elle ? Elle s’est confiée sur ses péripéties, plusieurs mois après le tournage.

Depuis plusieurs semaines maintenant, les bandes-annonces de L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 teasent l’épisode sur Justine à travers des extraits montrant notamment l’épreuve du speed dating. Ce lundi 14 septembre, le quatrième épisode, déjà disponible sur M6+, arrive donc enfin à la télévision, pour le plus grand bonheur des téléspectateurs. Et le moins que l’on puisse dire est que l’émission réserve bien des surprises, autant aux agriculteurs qu’aux fidèles du programme.

Dans l’épisode 4 de la saison 21 de L’Amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi soir dès 21 h 10 sur M6, Justine doit faire face à de nombreuses complications qui ont forcément impacté son aventure.

Sommaire

L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : le rendez-vous de Justine et Audran a viré au cauchemar…

Les spectateurs remarqueront que lors de son rendez-vous avec Audran, Justine n’est pas restée très immobile. En effet, à plusieurs reprises, la trentenaire a quitté le bateau pour prendre l’air. La raison ? Justine a le mal de mer. Malgré les précautions prises par la production, l’étape de la péniche était obligatoire pour le speed dating. Ainsi, l’agricultrice a dû faire face à ses peurs, mais cela n’a pas duré longtemps.

Interrogée par Télé Star sur cette expérience, Justine a déclaré qu’elle n’a malheureusement pas réussi à surmonter cette épreuve : « J’avais prévenu la production, mais j’ai pensé qu’en étant sur une péniche, à quai, sur la Seine, ça irait. Mais ça a été chaotique. Ça a tangué dans tous les sens, dans mon corps et dans ma tête. Les émotions étaient décuplées et je n’étais pas moi-même. Je lui ai fait vivre le pire date de toute sa vie« .

Voilà donc qui vient instantanément expliquer son comportement particulier envers Audran. Mais ce n’est pas tout ! Justine a également dû faire face à un désistement de dernière minute, qu’elle a encore du mal à digérer aujourd’hui…

Pourquoi Clément s’est désisté dans L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 ?

Alors que Justine s’apprêtait à annoncer à Audran et Clément qu’ils ont été choisis pour l’accompagner à la ferme, le prétendant de 24 ans et éducateur sportif, décide de prendre la main sur la situation en lui annonçant qu’il ne souhaite plus continuer l’émission à ses côtés. « C’était juste pour te dire que je ne vais pas donner suite malheureusement. Je n’ai pas eu ce petit coup de cœur même si tu es une nana magnifique. Je préfère stopper là et ne pas te donner de faux espoirs« , lui a alors annoncé Clément en face-à-face.

Toujours au micro de Télé Star, Justine n’a pas hésité à revenir sur cette trahison : « Ça m’a vraiment déçue. Pour moi, j’étais l’objet d’un pari avec ses copains, et j’ai trouvé ça dénigrant. » Justine était, en effet, tombée sous le charme de Clément, mais l’attirance n’était donc pas réciproque. À voir maintenant ce que l’avenir lui réserve au sein du jeu.

Drifa Maza

Journaliste

Journaliste chez Serieously depuis 2023, Drifa Maza est une grande passionnée de cinéma de toutes les époques, allant de ses débuts silencieux en noir et blanc à aujourd’hui. Toujours à l’affut de l’actualité, elle ne rate aucune sortie ciné et série, et est toujours à la recherche d’une nouveauté et d’un show à binger. Son enfance a été bercée par les films Pixar et l’ère Disney Channel, son adolescence par le genre de la dystopie et les Marvel (qu’elle aime toujours autant) mais c’est surtout en regardant La La Land en 2016 que son amour pour cette industrie est né. Aujourd’hui, Drifa adore partager cette passion et ses connaissances à travers des articles, des quiz et des interviews et rencontres avec les actrices, acteurs et cinéastes comme Celine Song, Danny Boyle ou encore Tom Hardy et Timothée Chalamet, qu’elle admire.
